object.title: The path-tree parse-word and level-restriction conjecture
object.statement: Let $n \geq 4$, and let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be $n$-leaf path trees such that leaf $1$ is on level $1$ in $T_1$ and leaf $n$ is on level $1$ in $T_2$. A pair is **mutually crooked** if it cannot be obtained by duplicating a leaf in a pair of $(n-1)$-leaf trees, and **weakly mutually crooked** if it cannot be obtained by triplicating a leaf in a pair of $(n-2)$-leaf trees. A **parse word** is a word that parses both trees. **Path-tree parse-word and level-restriction conjecture.** The following assertions hold: (i) if $T_1$ and $T_2$ have no parse word of the form $00v$ or $v00$, then they have a unique parse word up to permutation of the alphabet; (ii) if they have no parse word of the form $00v$ and are mutually crooked, then they have a parse word of the form $01v00$; (iii) if they have no parse word of the form $00v$, then the only possibilities for the pair of levels of leaves $2$ in $T_1$ and $n-1$ in $T_2$ are $(2,3)$ and $(k,2)$ for some $k \geq 2$; if they are weakly mutually crooked, one has $2 \leq k \leq 4$, and if they are mutually crooked, one has $2 \leq k \leq 3$. These claims are proposed as tools toward proving that every pair of binary trees has a parse word; the supplied text gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Bobbe Cooper, Eric Rowland and Doron Zeilberger, “Toward a language theoretic proof of the four color theorem”, arXiv:1006.1324 (2011).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.1324

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2010).

object.title: Combinatorial tropical gonality conjecture for lattice polygons
object.statement: Let $\Delta\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a two-dimensional lattice polygon, and let $\Delta^{(1)}$ denote the convex hull of the interior lattice points of $\Delta$. Write $\operatorname{lw}(\Delta^{(1)})$ for its lattice width, let $\Upsilon=\operatorname{Conv}\{(-1,-1),(1,0),(0,1)\}$, and let $\Gamma(\Delta_1,\ldots,\Delta_r)$ be the metric graph associated with a regular subdivision $\Delta_1,\ldots,\Delta_r$ of $\Delta$. **Combinatorial tropical gonality conjecture.** There exists a regular subdivision $\Delta_1,\ldots,\Delta_r$ of $\Delta$ such that the gonality of $\Gamma(\Delta_1,\ldots,\Delta_r)$ equals $\operatorname{lw}(\Delta^{(1)})+2$ if $\Delta\not\cong 2\Upsilon$, and equals $3$ if $\Delta\cong 2\Upsilon$. This combines the generic-gonality and lower-bound conjectures into a purely combinatorial statement; it is not established in general.
object.source_name: Wouter Castryck and Filip Cools, “Newton polygons and curve gonalities”, arXiv:1106.3762 (2012).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.3762

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2011).

object.title: Sign-reversing involution conjecture for plethysm coefficients
object.statement:
Let $\lambda$, $\mu$, and $\nu$ be partitions, let $l=l(\nu)$, and set

$$
A=\{(\pi,T)\mid \pi\in S_l,\ T\in\operatorname{SSTab}(\lambda[\mu];\pi*\nu)\},
$$

where $\pi*\nu=(\nu_{\pi(i)}-\pi_i+i)_{1\leq i\leq l}$. Let $\operatorname{SSTab}(\lambda[\mu])$ denote the relevant set of semistandard tableaux, and let $\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)$ be the sign of $\pi$.

**Sign-reversing cancellation conjecture.** There are a subset $S_0\subset\operatorname{SSTab}(\lambda[\mu])$ and a bijective map

$$
\phi\colon A\setminus A_0\longrightarrow A\setminus A_0
$$

such that, if $\phi(\pi,T)=(\pi',T')$, then $\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)=-\operatorname{sgn}(\pi')$, where

$$
A_0=\{(\pi,T)\in A\mid T\in S_0\}.
$$

Such a sign-reversing pairing would cancel all terms outside $A_0$ in the alternating formula $a_{\lambda[\mu]}^{\nu}=\sum_{(\pi,T)\in A}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)$ and would provide a combinatorial interpretation of the plethysm coefficient. The supplied text presents this as an expected conjecture and gives no evidence of a resolution.
object.source_name: Kazuto Iijima, “The first term of plethysms”, arXiv:1108.4915 (2011).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1108.4915

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2011).

object.title: Michael–Traves conjecture: the Roller Coaster Conjecture
object.statement:
Let $q$ be a positive integer, let $\pi$ be a permutation of $\{\lceil q/2\rceil,\lceil q/2\rceil+1,\ldots,q\}$, and let $i_k(G)$ denote the number of independent sets of cardinality $k$ in a graph $G$. A graph is **well-covered** if all its maximal independent sets have the same size, and $\alpha(G)$ denotes its independence number. **Roller Coaster Conjecture.** There is a well-covered graph $G$ with $\alpha(G)=q$ such that

$$
i_{\pi(\lceil q/2\rceil)}(G)<i_{\pi(\lceil q/2\rceil+1)}(G)<\cdots<i_{\pi(q)}(G).
$$

The paper proves this conjecture by constructing suitable well-covered graphs, so the asserted ordering is no longer open.
object.source_name: Jonathan Cutler and Luke Pebody, “Maximal-clique partitions and the Roller Coaster Conjecture”, arXiv:1412.4595 (2014).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2004–2014). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:math/0406623](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0406623).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.4595

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of December 2014); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

object.title: Shellability conjecture for k-cut complexes of hexagonal line tilings
object.statement:
Let $k$ be one of $4$, $5$, or $6$, and let $H$ be a hexagonal line tiling. Consider the $k$-cut complex of $H$.

**Hexagonal line tiling shellability conjecture.** For $k=4,5,$ and $6$, the $k$-cut complex of the hexagonal line tiling is shellable.

The conjecture is motivated by computational experiments using SageMath, which suggest that the behavior proved in the paper for $3$-cut complexes persists for these higher values of $k$. No resolution is given in the supplied source.
object.source_name: Himanshu Chandrakar, “On Shellability of 3-Cut Complexes of Hexagonal Grid Graphs”, arXiv:2512.21755 (2026).
object.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2004–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2407.08158](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.08158), [arXiv:2304.13675](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.13675), [arXiv:math/0401224](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0401224).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.21755

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

object.title: Dress's rank formula conjecture for 3-dimensional rigidity matroids
object.statement:
Let $G$ be an $\mathcal{R}_3$-closed graph, let $\hat{\mathcal{X}}$ be the set of maximal cliques in $G$ of size at least five, and let $F$ be the set of edges of $G$ not covered by $\hat{\mathcal{X}}$. For a collection $\mathcal{X}$ of vertex subsets, write $\deg_{\mathcal{X}}(h)$ for the number of sets containing the hinge $h$, and let $\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{X})$ be the set of hinges, namely pairs with degree at least two.

**The Dress Conjecture.** The rank of $G$ satisfies

$$
r_3(G)=|F|+\sum_{X\in \hat{\mathcal{X}}}(3|X|-6)-\sum_{h\in \mathcal{H}(\hat{\mathcal{X}})}(\deg_{\hat{\mathcal{X}}}(h)-1).
$$

The conjecture proposes a rank formula for $\mathcal{R}_3$-closed graphs. The analogous formula is known for the cofactor matroid $\mathcal{C}_2^1$, providing evidence, while the conjecture remains open for the 3-dimensional rigidity matroid.
object.source_name: Bill Jackson, Tibor Jordán and Soma Villányi, “Rank Contributions of Vertices in Rigidity Matroids of Clique Covered Graphs”, arXiv:2607.26266 (2026).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1104.4415](https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.4415).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26266

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).

object.title: A recursive upper-bound conjecture for graph partition weights
object.statement:
Let $\Pi(n,r)$ denote the quantity counting the relevant partitions or graph contributions, and let $C_{n,r}$ be the geometric factor associated with graphs having $r$ vertices and $n$ edges. Define

$$
\widetilde{\Pi}(n,r)=C_{n,r}\,\Pi(n,r).
$$

**Recursive upper-bound conjecture.** There exists a geometric constant $C<\infty$ such that

$$
\widetilde{\Pi}(n,r)\leq \widetilde{\Pi}(n-1,r-1)+C\,\widetilde{\Pi}(n-1,r)
$$

for $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$ with $n\geq r$, and with

$$
\widetilde{\Pi}(r,r)=C^r.
$$

The proposed bound is intended to exploit the decay of the edge factors $\Phi_{b,b'}$ in the graph expansion and thereby improve the factorial growth of the cruder estimate. The source presents this as a proposed recursive bound; no resolution is supplied here.
object.source_name: Domingos H. U. Marchetti and Roberto da Silva, “Brownian Motion Limit of Random Walks in Symetric Non-Homogeneous Media”, arXiv:math-ph/0404020 (2004).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math-ph/0404020

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2004).

object.title: Adjacency conjecture for partition m-hemimetrics
object.statement:
Let $V_n$ be the ground set, and let $\alpha(S_1,\dots,S_{m+1})$ and $\alpha(T_1,\dots,T_{m+1})$ be two partition $m$-hemimetrics on $V_n$. Two rays are adjacent when they generate a two-dimensional face of the cone, that is, when they are adjacent in the skeleton of $P_n^m$. **Adjacency conjecture for partition m-hemimetrics.** The two partition $m$-hemimetrics $\alpha(S_1,\dots,S_{m+1})$ and $\alpha(T_1,\dots,T_{m+1})$ are nonadjacent in the skeleton of $P_n^m$ if and only if there exist six different subsets $S_i,S_j,S_k$ and $T_{i'},T_{j'},T_{k'}$ such that

$$
S_i\mathbin{\cup}S_j=T_{k'}
$$

and

$$
S_k=T_{i'}\mathbin{\cup}T_{j'}.
$$

The conjecture holds for $m=1$, when all cut semimetrics are adjacent; for $n-m=2$, when the graph is $J(m+2,2)$; and for $(m,n)=(2,5)$ and $(3,6)$.
object.source_name: M. Deza and I. Rosenberg, “Small cones of m-hemimetrics”, arXiv:math/0005270 (2001).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0005270

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2000).

object.title: The First Borwein conjecture on the polynomials $A_n(q)$, $B_n(q)$ and $C_n(q)$
object.statement:
The polynomials $A_n(q)$, $B_n(q)$ and $C_n(q)$ are defined by

$$
\prod_{k=1}^n(1-q^{3k-2})(1-q^{3k-1})=A_n(q^3)-qB_n(q^3)-q^2C_n(q^3).
$$

**First Borwein conjecture.** The polynomials $A_n(q)$, $B_n(q)$ and $C_n(q)$ have nonnegative coefficients.

This is the observation communicated by P. Borwein to G. E. Andrews and is the motivating special case for the generalized Borwein conjecture. The source does not state whether it has been resolved.
object.source_name: S. Ole Warnaar, “The generalized Borwein conjecture. I. The Burge transform”, arXiv:math/0011220 (2000).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0011220

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2000).

object.title: The spanning conjecture for f-vectors of ordinary polytopes
object.statement:
Let $d$ be an odd integer with $d\ge 5$. An ordinary $d$-polytope is a polytope whose face structure is governed by the ordinary-polytope construction; write $f_i$ for the number of its $i$-dimensional faces. The **Euler hyperplane** is the affine hyperplane

$$
\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}f_i=2.
$$

**Spanning conjecture.** The set of $f$-vectors of all ordinary $d$-polytopes spans the Euler hyperplane. A spanning set consists of the ordinary polytopes

$$
P^{d,d+\lfloor i/2\rfloor,d+i},\qquad 1\le i\le d.
$$

This predicts that these explicitly specified ordinary polytopes provide enough $f$-vectors to span all admissible directions in the Euler hyperplane. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture is left open.
object.source_name: Margaret M. Bayer, Aaron M. Bruening and Joshua Stewart, “A combinatorial study of multiplexes and ordinary polytopes”, arXiv:math/0101076 (2001).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0101076

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2001).

object.title: Natural algebra action on matchings for alternating Kasteleyn matrices
object.statement: Let $A$ be a nonsingular alternating matrix, and let $D$ be the matrix-algebra deformation of $\mathbb{C}[\operatorname{coker} A]$ defined by the twisted relations in the paper. Let $G$ be a planar graph with nonempty matching set $P$, and suppose that $A$ is a Kasteleyn matrix of $G$. **Kasteleyn algebra-action conjecture.** There is a natural action of $D$ on $\mathbb{C}[P]$, possibly depending on how $G$ is embedded in the plane. Such an action would provide the algebraic structure underlying the proposed quantum-bijection interpretation of perfect matchings. The source gives no proof or resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
object.source_name: Greg Kuperberg, “Kasteleyn cokernels”, arXiv:math/0108150 (2002).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0108150

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2001).

object.title: The conjecture that knot-generated graphs differ from graphs with polynomial one
object.statement:
Let ${\cal C}_1$ be the set of graphs isotopic to planar graphs, ${\cal C}_2$ the set of graphs isotopic to graphs obtained from planar graphs by the specified moves, ${\cal C}_3$ the set of graphs isotopic to graphs obtained from knots, including the unknot, by those moves, and ${\cal C}_4$ the set of graphs whose polynomial $P$ equals $1$. The known inclusions are ${\cal C}_1\subseteq{\cal C}_2\subseteq{\cal C}_3\subseteq{\cal C}_4$.

**The conjecture that ${\cal C}_3$ and ${\cal C}_4$ differ.**

$$
{\cal C}_3\neq{\cal C}_4.
$$

This asserts that not every graph with polynomial $P=1$ can be obtained from a knot by the specified moves. The paper presents the question alongside the established inclusions but gives no proof or resolution of this separation.
object.source_name: Rui Pedro Carpentier, “Topological notions for Kauffman and Vogel's polynomial”, arXiv:math/0204207 (2002).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0204207

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2002).

object.title: Balanced-list maximization conjecture for the cd-index
object.statement:
Let $\beta(L)$ denote the beta-value associated with a list $L$. A list is **balanced** if its entries are either $k$ or $k+1$ for some non-negative integer $k$. Let $L$, $M$, and $L^{\prime}$ be lists. **Balanced-list maximization conjecture.** There exists a balanced list $B$ having the same degree and length as $M$ such that

$$
\beta(L,B,L^{\prime})\geq\beta(L,M,L^{\prime}).
$$

Thus, among lists with the prescribed degree and length in the middle position, a balanced list is conjectured to maximize the beta-value in every surrounding context; the source gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Swapneel Mahajan, “The cd-index of the Boolean lattice”, arXiv:math/0211390 (2002).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0211390

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2002).

object.title: Non-zero-divisor conjecture for Vogel's algebra Lambda
object.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be the graded commutative algebra formed from the antisymmetric subspace of connected tri-/univalent graphs with three labeled univalent vertices, and let $\Lambda_0$ be the subalgebra generated by $x_n$ for $n\geq 1$, with $x_1:=2t$ and $x_2:=t^2$. **Non-zero-divisor conjecture.** The map

$$
\Lambda_0\longrightarrow\Lambda_0,\qquad \lambda\longmapsto t\lambda
$$

is injective. Equivalently, $t$ is not a zero divisor in $\Lambda_0$. This assumption is used in the paper to obtain structural information about $\Lambda_0$, including a basis and an embedding into a subring of ${\mathbf{Z}}[t,u,v]$; the source gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Jan Kneissler, “On spaces of connected graphs II: Relations in the algebra Lambda”, arXiv:math/0301019 (2003).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0301019

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2003).

object.title: Littlewood–Richardson coefficient monotonicity under the starred transformation
object.statement:
Given an ordered pair $(\lambda,\mu)$ of partitions with the same number of parts, define

$$
\lambda^*_k=\lambda_k-k+\#\{\ell\mid \mu_\ell-\ell\geq\lambda_k-k\},
$$

and

$$
\mu^*_\ell=\mu_\ell-\ell+1+\#\{k\mid \lambda_k-k>\mu_\ell-\ell\}.
$$

For any partition $\nu$, **the starred-transformation conjecture.**

$$
c_{\,\lambda\,\mu}^{\,\nu}\leq c_{\,\lambda^*\,\mu^*}^{\,\nu}.
$$

This is a combinatorial conjecture about Littlewood–Richardson coefficients; the supplied text gives no resolution, and the surrounding discussion presents it as an open problem arising from a geometric approach.
object.source_name: Sergey Fomin, William Fulton, Chi-Kwong Li and Yiu-Tung Poon, “Eigenvalues, singular values, and Littlewood-Richardson coefficients”, arXiv:math/0301307 (2003).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0301307

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2003).

object.title: Conjecture on the linear coefficient of the Grassmannian Eulerian polynomial
object.statement:
For integers $k$ and $n$ in the range where the polynomial $\hat{E}_{k,n}(q)$ is defined, let $[q]\hat{E}_{k,n}(q)$ denote the coefficient of $q$ in $\hat{E}_{k,n}(q)$. **Linear-coefficient conjecture.**

$$
[q]\hat{E}_{k,n}(q) = {n \choose k+1}{n \choose k-2}.
$$

The polynomial $\hat{E}_{k,n}(q)$ is a $q$-analogue of the Eulerian numbers and interpolates between Eulerian, Narayana, and binomial numbers at $q=1$, $0$, and $-1$. This formula was motivated by experimental evidence, while comparable expressions for other coefficients were not known in the source.
object.source_name: Lauren K. Williams, “Enumeration of totally positive Grassmann cells”, arXiv:math/0307271 (2004).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0307271

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2003).

object.title: Extremal flow convergence conjecture for positive Kähler surfaces
object.statement: Let $(M,J)$ be a complex surface of positive first Chern class polarized by a Kähler class $\Omega$. The **positive first Chern class convergence conjecture.** There exists an initial condition for the extremal flow equation such that the solution exists on $[0,\infty)$ and, as $t\rightarrow\infty$, converges to an extremal metric of positive scalar curvature representing $\Omega$. This is a proposed global-existence and convergence statement for extremal metrics on positively polarized complex surfaces.
object.source_name: Santiago R. Simanca, “Heat Flows for Extremal Kähler Metrics”, arXiv:math/0310363 (2005).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0310363

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2003).

object.title: The adjacent-row bigrid perfection conjecture
object.statement:
Let a bigrid be an array with entries $\gamma(\epsilon,i,j)$, where the indices are taken wherever the entries are defined, and let a bigrid be **perfect** in the sense defined in the paper. **Adjacent-row bigrid perfection conjecture.** Any bigrid satisfying

$$
\gamma(1,i,j)=\gamma(0,i+1,j)
$$

whenever both sides are defined is perfect. The source notes that this conjecture is straightforward to verify when $m=n=2$, but gives no general resolution.
object.source_name: Eric M. Rains, “BC_n-symmetric abelian functions”, arXiv:math/0402113 (2006).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0402113

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2004).

object.title: The disjoint-path comparison conjecture for graded graphs
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a graded graph with root $\rho$, levels $V_0,\ldots,V_N$, and IID vertex labels with common distribution $\mu$. For an event $B$ of label sequences, let $P(G;B)$ be the probability that some graded path in $G$ has its label sequence in $B$. Let $M$ be the number of distinct graded paths in $G$, and let $G'$ consist of $M$ paths of length $N$ that are disjoint except at $\rho$. **Disjoint-path comparison conjecture.**

$$
P(G;B)\leq P(G';B).
$$

The comparison is known for graded graphs arising from trees, while the source reports only special cases for general graded graphs, including certain cases with $N=2$.
object.source_name: Robin Pemantle, “Tree-indexed processes”, arXiv:math/0404100 (2004).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0404100

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2004). “The most important open problem about tree-indexed processes is to get a converse to the Basic Theorem that would make the quasi-Bernoulli case as sharp as the Bernoulli case.”

object.title: Winding partitions conjecture for drawings of complete graphs
object.statement: Let $K_{3(q-1)+1}$ be the complete graph on $3(q-1)+1$ vertices, and consider any drawing of this graph in the plane. For a triangle of edges and a point not on it, its winding number about the point is the usual winding number of the closed triangular curve. **Winding partitions conjecture.** Every drawing has either $q-1$ pairwise disjoint triangles of edges and a vertex $v$, or $q-2$ pairwise disjoint triangles of edges and an intersection point $p$ of two edges, such that the winding number about $v$, respectively about $p$, of every triangle is nonzero. The conjecture is connected to the $d=2$ case of the general Tverberg-partition problem through geometric graph theory. The paper presents it as an equivalent formulation of that case; no resolution is given here.
object.source_name: Stephan Hell, “On the number of Tverberg partitions in the prime power case”, arXiv:math/0404406 (2004).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0404406

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2004).
